kurz: Baking is a balance: flour and egg give structure, sugar and fat make things tender and moist, air makes them light.
bild_im_kopf: Like a house built by two teams: one builds walls (flour, egg), the other makes it cosy (sugar, fat). Too much of one side and it turns tough or collapses.
was_passiert: Air gets into the batter through baking powder, baking soda, whisked-in air or steam. In the oven it expands until protein and starch set and hold the shape. Sugar and fat slow the [[glutenbildung|gluten network]], which is why cakes stay tender.
warum_wichtig: Baking is less forgiving than cooking, because amounts and order determine the structure. If you know the roles, you can still adapt.
faustregeln: Weigh rather than measure by volume.
Bring ingredients to room temperature when creaming butter.
Do not open the oven before the batter has set.
